mechanism_description: Ophthalmic timolol achieves 60-80% systemic bioavailability via nasolacrimal drainage, bypassing hepatic first-pass. Combined with oral atenolol, additive β-blockade causes excessive bradycardia and hypotension.
evidence_source: FDA Timoptic label: 'Additive effects of beta blockade may occur'; Drugs.com/Stockley's: timolol ophthalmic + oral beta-blockers = moderate-severe interaction

mechanism_description: Both timolol (β-blockade) and verapamil (Ca²⁺ channel blockade) suppress cardiac conduction and contractility. Combined use risks severe bradycardia, AV block, and heart failure.

mechanism_description: Brimonidine (α2-agonist) causes central sympatholysis and sedation. Fentanyl causes CNS and respiratory depression. Combined: profound sedation, hypotension, respiratory compromise. Documented in children with brimonidine alone.
